plain: To confirm officially in writing that something is true.

webster.text: To testify to in writing; to make a declaration in writing, under hand, or hand and seal, to make known or establish a fact.

example.quote: And they shall make a list of all the persons voted for, and of the number of votes for each; which list they shall sign and certify, and transmit sealed to the seat of the general government, directed to the president of the senate.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 12, 1787
